name: INTCALC.jcl
description:
The JCL job **INTCALC** executes program **CBACT04C** to calculate interest charges for credit card accounts as of the processing date **July 18, 2022** (passed as parameter `2022071800`). It reads transaction category balances, account cross-reference data, account details, and discount group definitions to compute interest, then writes the resulting interest transaction records to a new generation of a Generation Data Group (GDG) output file.Key Functionalities:
Reads transaction category balance data (TCATBALF) to identify per-category balances on which interest is to be calculated for each account.
Looks up card-to-account cross-reference information (XREFFILE and XREFFIL1) using both the primary KSDS path and the alternate index path to resolve card numbers to account numbers.
Retrieves account master data (ACCTFILE) to obtain account-level details such as credit limits, current balances, and account status needed for interest computation.
References discount group definitions (DISCGRP) to determine the applicable interest rates and discount rules for each account's transaction categories.
Generates a new sequential output file as the next generation (GDG +1) of **AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.SYSTRAN**, writing fixed-length 350-byte interest transaction records; the file is catalogued on success and deleted on failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Interest Calculation job is initiated for processing date July 18, 2022 and Cycle 00 (parameter: 2022071800), AND the following data sources are available and accessible: Account Data File (ACCTFILE) containing account statuses, credit limits, and outstanding balances; Card Cross-Reference File via primary index (XREFFILE) and alternate index path (XREFFIL1) for resolving card numbers to account numbers; Disclosure Group File (DISCGRP) containing applicable interest rates and fee structures per account group; Transaction Category Balance File (TCATBALF) containing balance summaries grouped by transaction category; AND a new generation of the System Transaction File (TRANSACT / SYSTRAN+1) is pre-allocated on disk to receive output records of fixed 350-character length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Program CBACT04C is executed with the processing date and cycle parameter '2022071800' to perform interest calculations across all eligible credit card accounts for that period
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: 1. Card numbers are resolved to their corresponding account numbers using the Card Cross-Reference File — first via the primary index (XREFFILE), and where needed via the alternate index path (XREFFIL1), ensuring all cards are matched to accounts; AND 2. For each eligible account, interest charges are calculated by combining the account's outstanding balances from the Account Data File (ACCTFILE), the applicable interest rates and fee structures from the Disclosure Group File (DISCGRP), and the transaction category-level balance summaries from the Transaction Category Balance File (TCATBALF); AND 3. Each calculated interest charge is written as a fixed 350-character transaction record to the new generation of the System Transaction File (SYSTRAN+1); AND 4. IF processing completes successfully, the new generation of the System Transaction File is cataloged and made permanently available for all downstream processing and reporting; AND 5. IF processing fails for any reason, the new generation of the System Transaction File is automatically deleted, ensuring no incomplete or erroneous interest transaction data is passed to downstream processes

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - CBACT04C - Credit Card Interest Calculation and Transaction Generation
rules.Rule_Description: This step invokes the Interest Calculator program (CBACT04C) for a specific processing date and cycle. It reads account balances, card-to-account cross-references, disclosure group interest rates, and transaction category balances to compute interest charges, then writes the resulting interest transactions to a new generation of the System Transaction File. The new file generation is preserved only if processing completes successfully; otherwise it is discarded automatically.
